newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima says Maastricht Treaty flexible enough.
newsitem.headline: Klima says Maastricht Treaty flexible enough.

text.p: Austrian chancellor Viktor Klima said on Monday he believed the Maastricht Treaty was sufficiently flexible to allow a sizeable start group for a single European currency.
In a speech at Vienna's diplomatic academy Klima said European economic and monetary union should "not be allowed to fail on 0.2 percent of GDP".

"As many European member states as possible should participate in the single currency from the start. That should be possible without altering the Maastricht Treaty. The Treaty is flexible enough," he said.
Klima reiterated that he expected the single European currency to start on time on January 1, 1999.

"It would be extremely perilous if EMU were to fail...It should be possible to implement the political project, without altering the criteria, by making use of the Treaty's flexibility," the chancellor said.
"We should not allow EMU to fail on 0.2 percent of GDP." -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
